response.title: Can I use a power station and charge it from solar panels at the same time?
response.answer:
Yes! Most modern portable power stations allow you to use them while simultaneously charging from solar panels. This is commonly called pass-through charging.

How it works
Solar power enters the station while it supplies electricity to your devices.

For example, suppose:

Solar panels generate 300W.

Your connected devices consume 200W.

The remaining approximately 100W can charge the battery, minus conversion losses.

If your devices consume 400W instead, the battery supplies the shortfall of approximately 100W, assuming the station supports that operating mode.

Important things to check

Pass-through charging support: Confirm your specific power station supports simultaneous solar charging and output.

Solar input limits: Your panels must stay within the station's permitted voltage, current, and wattage ranges.

Output capacity: Your connected devices must not exceed the station's rated output.

Battery behavior: Some models have limitations or may temporarily interrupt output when switching charging modes.

One question

What brand and model is your power station? (For example, EcoFlow DELTA 2, Jackery Explorer 1000, or Bluetti AC180.)

I can tell you whether your specific model supports simultaneous solar charging and power output, and what limitations apply.
